chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfaly, from al-Sakoony, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

A quadruped has six rights incumbent upon its owner: He should begin by feeding it when it stops, and offer it water whenever it passes by water. He should not strike its face, for it glorifies its Lord with its face. He should not ride on its back except in the way of God, Exalted and Mighty. He should not overload it beyond its capability, nor force it to walk more than it can.
ai.seo_question: What are the six rights of an animal over its owner in Shia Islamic tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* via the chain of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, this hadith codifies the six rights of quadrupeds, highlighting the theological nuance that the animal’s face is spared from striking because it 'glorifies its Lord' through its breathing. This tradition underscores the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and justice (*'adl*) extending to all creatures, linking physical care with spiritual reverence.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 6-28 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of Al-Nawfaly, on the authority of Al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad (MGB) , on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “

A quadruped has six rights incumbent upon his owner. When he stops, he should feed it first. He should give it water whenever it passes by water. He should not hit it on the face, since it glorifies God with its face. He should not ride on its back, unless it is in the way of God. He should not overload it beyond its capability. He should not force it to walk more than it can.”
